A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LIMOPro research work. All 26 pages, including Appendices A–B and the checklist, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PIR experiments on AIME, AMC, and GPQA Diamond, including benchmark comparisons, pruning and model-size analyses, and supplementary reasoning-pattern experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 3 and Appendix B, including Tables 2–3 and 6 and the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A retain the same reasoning-step segmentation, classification, perplexity-based importance scoring, and selective functional-step pruning. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use S1K, LIMO, and LIMO-V2 training data and evaluate on AIME24, AMC23, and GPQA Diamond. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2, 3, and 6, including the S1-PROMPT, S1-SPIRIT, and S1-RULE comparisons in Table 3.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same benchmark sizes, zero-shot CoT prompt, temperature of 0.7, correctness evaluator, and ACC/TOK/EFF metrics. Training procedures and the model-size, pruning-ratio, and token-budget settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The token-budget, pruning-ratio, and model-size analyses in Section 3.3 are unchanged, as are the reasoning-pattern comparisons and response case study in Appendices B.3–B.4.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight sampled responses per problem and retain the checklist statement that error bars and traditional significance tests are not reported. No seed, repeated-run, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 reports LIMO-P AIME accuracy of 63.3 and 10,588 average response tokens in both versions.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and PIR/perplexity definitions in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither the main text nor the appendices add or revise mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about selective refinement, improved accuracy with reduced token usage, and generalizability across data sources, model sizes, and token budgets.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning domain coverage, perplexity as an importance proxy, varying optimal pruning ratios, and access to closed-model perplexities.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, Appendix A prompts and pseudocode, dataset statistics, and code/data link are unchanged. The new funding acknowledgements provide no additional technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 4 and all 37 bibliography entries are unchanged. References move between pages because of the added acknowledgements, but no cited work or research-positioning argument changes.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 6, Acknowledgements, with reviewer thanks and funding disclosures, adds Pengfei Liu's SII affiliation, and replaces the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 publication notice. The research prose and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additional affiliation changes the title-page arrangement, and the acknowledgements shift reference placement across pages 10–12. Figures 1–9, Tables 1–6, and Algorithm 1 retain their content, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds affiliation, publication, and funding information with limited layout changes. The scientific exposition, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices, so these administrative additions do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
